entries.title: Active context, close, minimize, resize and descendants
entries.where: Master controller → Active context. Click the intended frame first.
entries.behavior: Actions target the clicked/focused frame. Esc steps out one field/popup level before minimizing; active MS has priority. W resizes/restores, M minimizes/restores, X closes, D toggles descendants, subject to saved bindings. Resized windows retain projected bounds and themed borders across focus and minimize/reopen. W restores retained original geometry. Projection styling is independent of React/Rnd wrapper updates.

steps.do: Open a frame, click a value field, edit it, then press Esc.
steps.expect: The value edit cancels and focus returns to its parent.

steps.do: Press Esc again at frame level; reopen it. Try M, W, then W again.
steps.expect: The frame minimizes/restores; resize can restore its earlier size.

steps.do: Expand several nested sections, then invoke Expand / collapse active descendants.
steps.expect: Descendant sections collapse together. Closing preserves reopenable frames.

steps.do: Resize with Shift+W, hover Full viewport and release Shift. Click the window body, minimize/re-expand it several times, then press W.
steps.expect: No extra white wrapper border or unexpected position jump. Expanded cycles return to the selected viewport; W restores original size and position.

entries.limits: Website viewport sizing, not OS/browser fullscreen. Pinned frames reject resizing. Projected frames use W restore before dragging, under the existing rigidity policy. User acceptance pending.

verification.browser: Focused floating-window and custom-frame cycles, body clicks, restored geometry and no browser border pass locally; user acceptance pending.

entries.title: Universal Shift configuration
entries.where: Hold Shift and press the configured shortcut of the function you want.
entries.behavior: Only relevant MC settings appear. Repeated shortcut presses cycle choices; hovering/focusing an option selects the temporary choice. Release Shift applies the selected choice once. Right-click applies and locks it; left-click resets to priority 1. Hover/focus does not change the saved default.

steps.do: Activate a frame. Hold Shift, press W, then hover a different resize level without pressing W again. Release Shift.
steps.expect: The pointed option becomes selected and previews its bounds; Shift release applies that option exactly once. Keyboard focus selects an option the same way.

steps.do: Repeat Shift+W, right-click another option, release Shift, then use plain W. Repeat and left-click an option.
steps.expect: Right-click applies and locks once; later Shift release does not execute again. Plain W uses the locked level or restores an active projection. Left-click resets to priority 1.

entries.limits: Shift release executes only an armed shortcut configuration. Explicit button-opened configuration remains unarmed. User acceptance pending.

entries.title: Move, dock, select and organize UI
entries.where: UI library; UI edit mode; shared frame/control context actions.
entries.behavior: Drag actual frame handles or supported control edges. Docking offers destinations when a dragged header reaches another header. UI selection, alignment, compaction and reset are separate from knowledge structure. Window/frame drag previews reuse gesture-local target discovery and read-only docking policy results. Visual movement uses the latest pointer position once per animation frame, with geometry reads before transform writes. Release refreshes destination geometry and commits through the existing shared history; cancellation restores the live payload. Active-context shortcuts defer to a held UI gesture, so Esc cancels the drag before a parent minimize action. Pickup snapshots exclude descendants of the held frame/window and read visibility before lifting, reducing the expand-then-drag setup burst.

steps.do: Create a UI frame, then drag a complete section into it by its handle.
steps.expect: Its live controls move with it.

steps.do: Hover another window without dragging; then drag a header over another header and choose a dock guide.
steps.expect: Hover alone offers no docking. The deliberate drop docks the frame.

steps.do: Select multiple UI controls and invoke Compact selected UI / Align UI. Undo.
steps.expect: Selected controls rearrange; undo restores their UI arrangement without changing graph facts.

steps.do: In UI edit mode, drag an expanded floating window across empty canvas, release it, then Undo once. Start another drag and press Esc before release.
steps.expect: The window follows the latest pointer position. Release saves its final location; one Undo restores the prior layout. Esc cancels movement without saving a layout change. Report any visible frame skipping.

entries.limits: Drag targets use a gesture-local discovery snapshot, refreshed at release. Browser traces are local diagnostics; user hardware smoothness acceptance remains pending.

entries.title: Ordered operations, role picking, target repair and count extraction
entries.where: Composer → Scope / Ordered operations.
entries.behavior: Count, scale, fill, rotate, select, connect and oscillate run in order. Picked roles scope new operations; flow selection otherwise applies. Missing generated roles remain unresolved until explicitly repaired. Highlight units / region selects a 1-based unit or all scoped units and highlights an exact disk sector/ring arc fraction. Rotate supports highlighted region, each unit and group scopes, target-center/origin/custom pivots, saved snap step/origin and optional allowed angles. Rotate one step is rebindable and inherits Shift configuration. Operation tools are canonical scope-relative recipes, saved from the focused operation and applied as editable snapshots to picked/flow scope.

steps.do: Add Count followed by Extract count; change Count.
steps.expect: The extracted scalar reflects the preceding count operation.

steps.do: Move Extract count before Count using the order controls.
steps.expect: Its scalar now reflects the earlier state.

steps.do: Target a generated unit, shrink count so it disappears, then use picked scope / repair targets.
steps.expect: The missing role is reported, never silently redirected, and an explicit replacement repairs it.

steps.do: Open Create → New Omnic object. In Preset choose Member · one of two. Select Highlight units / region in Ordered operations.
steps.expect: Two generated dots remain; Unit 1 is highlighted. Change Unit to 2 to move the highlight without drawing or changing unit count.

steps.do: Choose Part · half a unit. Its highlight has fraction 0.5. Add Rotate structure, set Rotate to Highlighted region and Snap step to 30°. Set Angle to 50°.
steps.expect: The half highlight rotates to 60°; the dot stays fixed. Together rotates the scoped composition; Each unit rotates each shape about its own center. Earlier operations determine the region available.

steps.do: Set Snap step to 30° and use Rotate one step. Rebind that action in Master controller shortcuts if desired; hold Shift with its configured trigger to edit rotation configuration.
steps.expect: Each ordinary invocation advances the angle by its saved snap. Repeated Shift trigger cycles Region → Each unit → Together; release applies. Right-click applies/locks; left-click resets to the first scope. Temporary changed configuration adds a scoped rotation operation and preserves the focused settings.

steps.do: Focus Highlight units / region, set a copy name and choose Save operation as tool. Return to a composition, pick a component or Whole structure, open Reusable tools, choose the saved tool and Stamp copy to scope.
steps.expect: The tool is a shared canonical object with no generated units. Applying it adds independently editable operations to the current draft; changing the tool later does not retroactively change stamped operations. Save shared, reopen and Undo/Redo retain authored rules.

entries.limits: Browser acceptance has not been recorded for this guide. Fractions are angular sectors of disks or arc fractions of rings; fractional lines report inapplicable. Whole line highlight works. One highlight layer per primitive (later highlight replaces earlier). Rotation is planar, angles bounded ±1080°, snap step 0–360°, up to 32 allowed-angle values. New rotation operators use target center; legacy operators retain origin/pivot offsets. Tool stamping snapshots operations rather than introducing live executable dependencies. No default rotation shortcut is assigned. Fixed-size world reading integration remains deferred.

entries.title: Atomnic placement, selection, contextual DOFs and pivot rotation
entries.where: Create → New Omnic object opens Atomnic; existing Composer → Atomnic mode. Right-click the local construction surface or active edited world image.
entries.behavior: Right-click the construction or edited world image reveals only applicable functions with current values. Left-click uses retained settings; right-click ONE function opens only its first relevant setter. Next/Confirm advances one input at a time; Back/Esc goes back. There is no permanent function toolbar or expanded settings grid. Rotation configures scope → angular order → step count, then prompts for a pivot. During pivot picking, right-click reveals exact/detected choices; right-click Detected target to configure axis then position progressively. Existing construction, Free/touching, selection, marking, history and live preview remain available.

steps.do: Create a new Omnic object. Move the pointer over the local square, click a neighboring slot, then hold and sweep.
steps.expect: A ghost follows legal slots; individual units are placed on a non-overlapping triangular lattice. The world updates before Save shared.

steps.do: Open New Omnic object; inspect the construction, then right-click a unit. Left-click Select; Shift-click another unit, then G and drag. Right-click → Group; right-click Select to change Scope to Macro.
steps.expect: No function toolbar is shown initially. Right-click shows only function entries with retained values; Select configuration shows only Scope. Grouped units then move together under Macro.

steps.do: Right-click the construction, then RIGHT-click Draw. Advance through its individual setters: choose Free at Constraints, then choose imprint radius and independent movement step. Confirm and sweep.
steps.expect: Exactly one relevant input is visible per step; later setters are unmounted until Next. Fine, overlapping or spaced imprints are possible. Touching mode keeps movement coupled and skips its independent-step setter.

steps.do: Select a unit/group; right-click the construction, then RIGHT-click Rotate (or press R while the function list is open). Confirm Scope, angular order 1, then step 1.
steps.expect: Only one of those setters appears at a time. Final Confirm closes configuration and prompts for the pivot. Ordinary R outside the menu skips setters and uses retained settings. Exact/detected mode choices appear only on right-click during pivot picking.

steps.do: During pivot picking, right-click → RIGHT-click Detected target. Right-click Axis; choose Top as first boundary, Right as second, then halving depth 1. At the following Position prompt choose depth 2 and axis start.
steps.expect: Bounds, depth, optional direction and position appear in sequence. Depth 1 accepts the midpoint without a direction question. Depth 2 requires direction. The reference is retained and the UI returns to the target-picking prompt; unsupported angular precision is rejected rather than rounded silently.

steps.do: For Member place two units, select one, right-click the construction then RIGHT-click Highlight. Confirm Scope, fraction 1, orientation, contrasting color and opacity in sequence. Repeat on one unit with fraction 1/2 for Part.
steps.expect: Only the current highlight setter appears, and confirmation applies the mark. A normal left-click Highlight subsequently uses those retained settings immediately.

steps.do: Right-click a unit → Property patterns. Hover Size or Color; select a row, combine + and − criteria; use selectionUndo then selectionRedo.
steps.expect: Candidate sets glow, ranked registered properties select matching units without comparing absolute position, include/exclude refines the set, and selection history changes no geometry.

steps.do: Repeat a move or rotation on the active world image. Release, undo the accepted edit, close/reopen, then Save shared.
steps.expect: Both editing surfaces use the same draft. Pointer samples stay transient, release records an accepted edit, close restores saved world rendering, reopening recovers work and save publishes the definition.

entries.limits: 128 components/groups and 128 operations; coordinates ±300. Authored dot/group recipes plus highlights only; arrays/references/other geometry operations keep Generator controls. Shared matcher currently covers dot properties, not full MS clipping or arbitrary motifs. The selected axis is not manually guessed: boundary halving resolves it. Full world-space radial boundary gestures remain pending. Touching validates center slots/radius overlap, not stroke width or full physics. World budget 32 sources/256px/12fps. Max-zoom calibration and circular frame/dials are pending.

entries.title: Click responsiveness and shared rendering work
entries.where: Ordinary controls, including Omnic library → Objects → Structural filters.
entries.behavior: Render-time function, anchor, owner and icon target lookups share snapshot indexes. Opening/collapsing a frame preserves appearance target metadata when ownership and captions are unchanged. Appearance adjusters reuse target calculations; hidden dock areas skip measurement. Hot function controls now subscribe to their own item, binding, selection and permission slices instead of the full UI context. Stable appearance context actions keep current handlers without broadcasting closure changes. Legacy consumers retain their existing route during incremental migration. Fields, action registrations and embedded headers use scoped subscriptions. Dock workspace geometry/context preserve identity when unchanged; appearance label invalidation follows actual customized owners, not unrelated frame registration order. Floating windows, panels, frame chrome, docking residents and labels now use scoped subscriptions. Closed frame searches and dormant popup adapters do not subscribe to unrelated UI updates. Native caption/button discovery deduplicates inserted subtrees and updates changed hosts directly; unchanged native presentation skips DOM writes and permission work. Discovered function registrations publish once per microtask while commands/history remain synchronous. With no UI controls selected, ordinary layout changes now skip UI-selection discovery and visibility measurement. Subscription snapshot checks reuse pure selector results for the same committed snapshot and selector; changed state or captured props still reevaluate. Window movement now coalesces pointer positions per frame, reuses target lists and caches ownership/pinning/context/docking reads until the layout snapshot changes. Final release refreshes the pointed destination and uses the existing single-commit history path. Newly discovered frame captions now read their initial font sizes together before symbol/tooltip styling writes. This avoids repeated synchronous style recalculation during first-use presentation; later collapse/reopen keeps existing caption state. Drag pickup excludes a frame/window’s own subtree from destination measurements, snapshots visibility before lifting, and uses an exact resident lookup. Final destination refresh and shared docking/history remain intact. Repeated activation of the current front window reuses its existing layer rather than changing z-index and rerendering the wrapper on each grab; other windows still rise. Fixed surfaces already mounted directly on the page move using their existing transform without popover promotion or geometry rewrites. Drag destination bounds are cached on demand; child-slot measurement is limited to destinations actually considered. Cursor-open windows use viewport free placement on both rendering and drop, avoiding workspace packing on release. Drag capture no longer toggles a descendant CSS selector across the whole page. Release deduplicates pointed ancestor measurements, reuses gesture candidate lists. Final placement continues to use the exact release coordinate; no inertia is implemented. Moving an already-free frame validates its new coordinates and preserves unrelated layout records instead of rerunning structural detach/prune/full validation. The held payload now receives a direct transform update from each pointer event; docking discovery/feedback alone stays frame-batched. Movement does not wait for docking calculations or interpolate toward the cursor. Release now hands direct visual ownership back to committed layout synchronously, preventing a paint of the pre-drag position between them. The interface state owner recognizes immutable coordinate-only edits and validates the changed coordinates without rechecking unchanged topology; other edits/imports retain full validation.
